questions.question: Due to the festive season, a shopkeeper offers 20% discount. Another discount of 5% is offered to customers who make a purchase of more than Rs. 5,000. Anupam purchased items marked for Rs. 7,500. How much did he save?
questions.solution:
Given:

Due to the festive season, a shopkeeper offers 20% discount. 

Another discount of 5% is offered to customers who make a purchase of more than Rs. 5,000. 

Anupam purchased items marked for Rs. 7,500.

Concept used:

Discount = Marked price × Discount%

Discount% = {(Marked Price - Selling Price) over Marked Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Final discount = 20 + 5 - (20 × 5)/100 = 24%

Discount given to Anupam = 7500 × 24%

⇒ Rs. 1800

∴ He saved Rs. 1800.

questions.question: The compound interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 8% per annum compounded annually is Rs. 416. What is the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for the same period?
questions.solution:
Given:

The compound interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 8% per annum compounded annually is Rs. 416.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

In case of the compound interest,

Amount = P(1 + R/100)N

CI = P(1 + R/100)N - P

Calculation:

Let the sum be Rs. Q.

According to the question,

Q(1 + 8/100)² - Q = 416

⇒ 0.1664Q = 416

⇒ Q = 416/0.1664

⇒ Q = 2500

Now, the simple interest on Rs. 2500 for 2 years at 8% per annum

⇒ (2500 × 8 × 2)/1000 = Rs. 400

**∴ Rs. 400 is the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for the same period.**

questions.question: Abhay sold 70% of his goods at a profit of 25%, 40% of the remaining goods at a loss of 40%, and the remaining goods at the cost price. What was his profit/loss percentage in the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
Given:

Abhay sold 70% of his goods at a profit of 25%, 40% of the remaining goods at a loss of 40%, and the remaining goods at the cost price.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let there be 100 items and each cost Rs. 100.

Total cost price = 100 × 100 = Rs. 10000

Selling of the goods sold at a 70% profit = (100 × 70%) × (100 + 100 × 25%)

⇒ 70 × 125 = Rs. 8750

Selling of the goods sold at a 40% loss = ((100 - 70) × 40%) × (100 - 100 × 40%)

⇒ 12 × 60 = Rs. 720

Selling of the goods sold at the cost price = (100 - 70 - 12) × 100 

⇒ Rs. 1800

Total selling price = 8750 + 720 + 1800 = Rs. 11270

Now, the profit percentage = {{11270 - 10000} over 10000} × 100\%

⇒ 12.7%

**∴ His profit percentage in the entire transaction was 12.7%.**

questions.question: A person invested (1)/(2) of his capital at 6%, (1)/(4) at 8% and the remaining at 12%. If his annual income is Rs. 528, then find the capital.
questions.solution:
Given:

A person invested (1)/(2) of his capital at 6%, (1)/(4) at 8% and the remaining at 12%.

His annual income is Rs. 528.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where, P = Principal amount, R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the capital be Rs. 8x.

Interest on (1)/(2) of his capital at 6% = (8x/2 × 6 × 1)/100

⇒ Rs. 6x/25

Interest on (1)/(4) of his capital at 8% = (8x/4 × 8 × 1)/100

⇒ Rs. 4x/25

Remaining capital = 8x - 4x - 2x = Rs. 2x

Interest on his remaining capital at 12% = (2x × 12 × 1)/100

⇒ Rs. 6x/25

According to the question,

6x/25 + 4x/25 + 6x/25 = 528

⇒ 16x/25 = 528

⇒ x = (528 × 25)/16

⇒ x = 825

⇒ 8x = 6600 (Multiplying 8 on both sides)

∴ The capital was Rs. 6600.

questions.question: 5 women and 2 men can complete a work in 4 days, while 6 women and 3 men can complete the same work in 3 days. How many days will one woman and one man working together take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

5 women and 2 men can complete a work in 4 days, while 6 women and 3 men can complete the same work in 3 days. 

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day (Efficiency) × Total time taken

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of a man and woman be M and W respectively.

According to the question,

(5W + 2M) × 4 = (6W + 3M) × 3

⇒ 20W + 8M = 18W + 9M

⇒ 2W = M

⇒ M = 2W ....(1)

Total work = (5W + 2M) × 4

⇒ 20W + 8M

⇒ (20W + 8 × 2W) (From 1)

⇒ (20W + 16W)

⇒ 36W

Efficiency of one man and one woman = M + W

⇒ 2W + W = 3W

Now, time taken by one man and one woman to complete the task = 36W/3W

⇒ 12 days

**∴ In 12 days one woman and one man working together will take to complete the same work.**

questions.question: The average price of 10 books is Rs. 150, while the average price of 8 of these books is Rs. 135. Of the remaining 2 books, if the price of one book is 40% more than the price of the other book, thea what is the price of the costlier of these two books?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average price of 10 books is Rs. 150, while the average price of 8 of these books is Rs. 135. 

Of the remaining 2 books, the price of one book is 40% more than the price of the other book.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Total price of the 8 books = 8 × 135 = Rs. 1080

Total price of all 10 books = 10 × 150 = Rs. 1500

Let the price of one of the books be Rs. Q.

Other of the other book = Q + Q × 40% = Rs. 1.4Q

According to the question,

Q + 1.4Q = 1500 - 1080

⇒ 2.4Q = 420

⇒ Q = 420/2.4

⇒ Q = 175

Now, the price of the costlier book = 1.4 × 175

⇒ Rs. 245

∴ The price of the costlier book is Rs. 245.

questions.question: If by subtracting 35% of a number from the number the result is 26, then what is the number?
questions.solution:
Given:

By subtracting 35% of a number from the number the result is 26.

Calculation:

Let the number be Q.

According to the question,

Q - Q × 35% = 26

⇒ Q - 0.35Q = 26

⇒ 0.65Q = 26

⇒ Q = 26/0.65

⇒ Q = 40

∴ The required number is 40.

questions.question: If P ∶ Q = 3 ∶ 2, then find the ratio (P² - Q²) ∶ (P² + Q²).
questions.solution:
Given:

P ∶ Q = 3 ∶ 2

Calculation:

P : Q = 3 : 2

⇒ P² : Q² = 9 : 4 (Squaring both sides)

⇒ (P² + Q²)/(P² - Q²) = (9 + 4)/(9 - 4) (Using componendo-dividendo method)

⇒ (P2 + Q2)/(P2 - Q2) = 13/5

⇒ (P2 - Q2)/(P2 + Q2) = 5/13

⇒ (P2 - Q2) : (P2 + Q2) = 5 : 13

**∴ (P2 - Q2) ∶ (P2 + Q2) is equal to 5 : 13.**

questions.question: In a competitive examination, the ratio of qualified boys and girls is 3 ∶ 2. If one more boy qualifies, and one qualified girl leaves the class, then their new ratio becomes 2 ∶ 1. What is the initial total sum of the qualified candidates?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a competitive examination, the ratio of qualified boys and girls is 3 ∶ 2. 

If one more boy qualifies, and one qualified girl leaves the class, then their new ratio becomes 2 ∶ 1. 

Calculation:

Let there be 3x and 2x number of qualified boys and girls respectively.

Total qualified candidates = 2x + 3x = 5x

According to the question,

(3x + 1) : (2x - 1) = 2 : 1

⇒ 3x + 1 = 4x - 2

⇒ 4x - 3x = 2 + 1

⇒ x = 3

⇒ 5x = 15 (Multiplying 5 on both sides)

∴ The initial sum of the qualified candidates is 15.

questions.question: The savings of Rita is equal to 20% of her expenditure. If her income increases by 35% and expenditure increases by 38%, then ber savings:
questions.solution:
Given:

The savings of Rita is equal to 20% of her expenditure.

Concept used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Calculation:

Let the expenditure of of Rita be Rs. 100

Savings = 100 × 20% = Rs. 20

Income = 20 + 100 = Rs. 120

Increased income = 120 + 120 × 35%

⇒ Rs. 162

Increased expenditure = 100 + 100 × 38%

⇒ Rs. 138

New savings = 162 - 138 = Rs. 24

Now, % increase = {{24 - 20} over 20} times 100\%

⇒ 20%

**∴ If her income increases by 35% and expenditure increases by 38%, then her savings increases by 20%.**

questions.question: A person travels one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h, and the remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h. If he travels this distance at a uniform speed taking the same time, then what will be his speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
Given:

A person travels one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h, and the remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h. 

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Average speed = Total distance covered ÷ Total time taken

Calculation:

Let the distance be 3D km.

Time taken to complete one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h

⇒ (3D × 1/3) ÷ 45

⇒ D/45 hours

Remaining distance = 3D - D = 2D km

Time taken to complete remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h

⇒ 2D ÷ 60

⇒ D/30 hours

Now, his speed will be = 3D over {{Dover 45} + {D over 30}}

⇒ 3 over {1 over 18} = 54 km/h

∴ His speed will be 54 km/h.

questions.question: A train takes a certain time to cover a certain distance at a uniform speed of 70 km/h. If the train runs at a speed of 65 km/h, then it takes 42 minutes more than before. What is the distance (in km) covered by the train?
questions.solution:
Given:

A train takes a certain time to cover a certain distance at a uniform speed of 70 km/h. If the train runs at a speed of 65 km/h, then it takes 42 minutes more than before.

Concept used:

1 hour = 60 minutes

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Let the distance be D km.

According to the question,

D/65 - D/70 = 42/60

⇒ D/910 = 7/10

⇒ D = 7 × 91

⇒ D = 637

∴ The distance covered by the train is 637 km.

questions.question: Numerically, what percentage of its circumference is the area of a circle of radius 4?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius = 4

Concept used:

Area of a circle = πr²

Circumference of the circle = 2πr

Where r = radius of the circle

Calculation:

Circumference of the circle = 2π × 4 = 8π

Area of the circle = π × 4² = 16π

Now, % = 16π/8π × 100%

⇒ 200%

**∴ Numerically, 200% of its circumference is the area of a circle of radius 4.**

questions.question: The HCF of two 4-digit numbers is 103 and their LCM is 19261. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
Given:

The HCF of two 4-digit numbers is 103 and their LCM is 19261.

Concept used:

HCF of two or more numbers is the greatest factor that divides the numbers.

LCM is the smallest common multiple of two or more numbers.

Calculation:

Let the numbers be 103p and 103q respectively.

According to the question,

LCM (103p, 103q) = 19261

⇒ 103 × p × q = 19261

⇒ pq = 187

So, pq = 11 × 17

Since 11 and 17 are co-prime to each other, the numbers (103 × 11) i.e. 1133 and (103 × 17) i.e. 1751.

Now, the sum = 1133 + 1751

⇒ 2884

∴ The sum of the two numbers is 2884.
